newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan closes slightly up against US dollar.
newsitem.headline: Yuan closes slightly up against US dollar.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed up slightly at 8.3064 on Friday from Thursday's 8.3066 against the U.S. dollar on the Shanghai-based interbank foreign exchange market in dull trading, traders said.
The yuan opened up at 8.3063 and consolidated in the range of 8.3060 and 8.3066 for most of the session, hitting an intra-day low of 8.3069 early and a sudden high of 8.3056 in late trade.
Trading was dull, with most done at 8.3064, traders said.
Dealers said that, although the yuan was stable, the market expect it to rise again.
Zhou Xiaochuan, director-general of China's State Administration of Exchange Control, said on Thursday the yuan was facing pressure to appreciate because of falling inflation.

China's trade and non-trade surplus and inflow of foreign investment make demand for yuan much larger than supply, which supported its upward movement, he said. Dealers expect the yuan to move in the range of 8.3050-8.3070 early next week.
The yuan closed almost unchanged at 7.6512 from 7.6525 against 100 Japanese yen and down at an intraday low of 1.0751 from 1.0745 against the Hong Kong dollar.
